tagline: Advance Auto Parts, Inc. is an American automotive aftermarket parts retailer focused on delivering quality products and services to DIY and professional customers.
hero_kpi_rationale: Gross margin is the primary indicator of profitability in the automotive parts distribution sector, reflecting the company's ability to manage cost of goods sold relative to sales.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Percentage of revenue remaining after deducting cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Gross margin increased by 592 basis points in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily due to the negative impact on gross margin in 2024 from inventory charges related to the 2024 Restructuring Plan.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in gross margin driven by reduced inventory-related charges.

kpis.name: Net Sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated from sales after deductions for returns and discounts.
kpis.description: Net sales decreased by 5.4% in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily due to lower sales resulting from store closures executed under the 2024 Restructuring Plan, partially offset by the impact of the 53rd week.
kpis.signal: Decline in revenue due to store closures, partially offset by an additional week.

kpis.name: Operating Loss
kpis.explanation: Loss resulting from the company's core operations before interest and taxes.
kpis.description: Operating loss improved by $670 million in 2025 compared to 2024, primarily attributable to lower restructuring and related charges in 2025 versus 2024. Operating loss represented (0.5)% of net sales in 2025.
kpis.signal: Significant improvement in operating loss due to reduced restructuring charges.

kpis.name: Comparable Store Sales
kpis.explanation: Increase in sales from stores open for at least one year.
kpis.signal: Slight growth in sales from existing stores.

kpis.name: Restructuring Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs associated with corporate reorganization and transformation plans.
kpis.description: Restructuring and related expenses amounted to $204 million in 2025, compared to $309 million in 2024, a 34% decrease.
kpis.signal: Significant reduction in restructuring expenses compared to the prior year.

kpis.name: Self-Insurance Reserves
kpis.explanation: Amount set aside to cover future insurance claims not covered by external policies.
kpis.description: The company's self-insurance reserves totaled $156 million as of January 3, 2026, compared to $141 million as of December 28, 2024, an increase of 10.6%.
kpis.signal: Increase in self-insurance reserves, reflecting potential rise in future risks or costs.

kpis.name: Excess and Obsolete Inventory Reserve
kpis.explanation: Amount reserved for inventory that can no longer be sold at cost or normal price.
kpis.description: The excess and obsolete inventory reserve was $68 million as of January 3, 2026, compared to $302 million as of December 28, 2024, including $18 million related to inventory write-downs from the 2024 Restructuring Plan.
kpis.signal: Drastic reduction in obsolete inventory reserve, linked to restructuring activities.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $8.601 billion in the latest fiscal year (FY2026).

kpis.name: Restructuring and Related Expenses
kpis.explanation: Costs incurred during the implementation of restructuring plans.
kpis.description: Restructuring and related expenses decreased by 34% in 2025 compared to 2024, declining from $309 million to $204 million.
kpis.signal: Decline in restructuring expenses indicates a gradual exit from transformation activities.

kpis.name: Excess and Obsolete Inventory Reserve
kpis.explanation: Provision for inventory that has become unsellable or has declined in value.
kpis.description: The excess and obsolete inventory reserve was reduced by 77.5% in 2025, from $302 million to $68 million, partly due to write-downs related to the restructuring plan.
kpis.signal: Sharp reduction in this reserve suggests improved inventory management and the impact of restructuring.

risks.title: Costly and Disruptive Restructuring
risks.summary: Store closures, workforce reductions, and adjustment costs threaten operational stability despite expected future gains.
risks.score_rationale: The 2024 restructuring plan is central in the 10-K, with charges of $309M in 2024 and $204M in 2025, strong language on operational impact. Existential risk tied to deep business model transformation. Industrial category heavily weighted. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Dependence on a Bankrupt Supplier
risks.summary: The bankruptcy of a major supplier exposes the company to credit losses and supply disruptions, even though purchases are now marginal.
risks.score_rationale: Explicit mention of a key supplier in Chapter 11 bankruptcy, with a non-cash charge of $28M. Cautious language on continuity risks. High placement in recent risk disclosures, Supply Chain category moderately weighted. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Import Tariff Pressures
risks.summary: New tariffs on imported parts increase costs, threatening margins if price increases cannot be passed through to customers.
risks.score_rationale: New customs tariffs on imports from Canada, China, and Mexico are mentioned early in the report. Alert language on potential future changes. Geopolitical category moderately weighted, but risk on the rise. (default score, to be refined)

risks.title: Ongoing Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: Inflation in transportation, labor, and supply costs weighs on profitability and customer purchasing power.
risks.score_rationale: Inflation cited in the 'Industry Update' section as a key factor affecting logistics and wage costs. Recurring language integrated into macro risks. Macro category heavily weighted, central in analysis. (default score, to be refined)

ai_positioning.summary: No significant mention of artificial intelligence, machine learning, or related technologies was found in the 10-K filing.
